title: After-hours work communication policies and employee well-being
asked: Dr Charlene Chen asked what data MOM collects on after-hours work expectations and digital connectivity, what assessment it has made of workplace policies on after-hours communication, and whether it will study links between hyper-connectivity, family life and fertility intentions. Dr Hamid Razak asked whether MOM has reviewed how the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-Being at Workplaces is implemented in relation to after-hours work communications, and what findings emerged.
asked_by: Dr Charlene Chen and Dr Hamid Razak
response: MOM monitors adoption of after-hours communication practices: in 2025, 55% of full-time resident employees reported their employers had such policies, up from 48% in 2022, covering practices such as not expecting replies to non-urgent messages until the next working day or time-off-in-lieu for after-hours work. MOM has not conducted a separate assessment of the effectiveness of each individual policy. It points to the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony, the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces and the iWorkHealth tool, and says a Marriage and Parenthood Reset Workgroup has been set up.

key_points.point: In 2025, 55% of full-time resident employees reported their employers had policies governing after-hours communication, up from 48% in 2022.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: in 2025, 55% of full-time resident employees reported that their employers had policies governing after-hours communication

key_points.point: These policies include not expecting responses to non-urgent messages until the next working day, or time-off-in-lieu for after-hours work.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: not expecting responses to non-urgent messages until the next working day or providing time-off-in-lieu for after-hours work

key_points.point: MOM has not conducted a separate assessment of the effectiveness of each individual policy.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: We have not conducted a separate assessment of the effectiveness of each of these individual policies.

key_points.point: The approach is not to focus on connectivity itself but on the broader impact on employee well-being and workplace practices.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Our approach is not to focus on the connectivity per se but on the broader impact on employee well-being and workplace practices.

key_points.point: The iWorkHealth tool helps employers identify workplace stressors and psychosocial risks employees may face.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: such as the iWorkHealth, which helps employers identify the workplace stressors and psychosocial risks that employees may be subject to

key_points.point: A Marriage and Parenthood Reset Workgroup has been set up to develop a whole-of-society approach to marriage and parenthood journeys.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: A Marriage and Parenthood Reset Workgroup has also been set up to develop a whole-of-society approach to better support Singaporeans in their marriage and parenthood journeys.

key_points.point: MOM is monitoring developments in other jurisdictions, including those with codes of practice, and will study and adapt useful practices for Singapore's context.
key_points.speaker: unattributed
key_points.quote: we are monitoring the situation and developments in other jurisdictions including those who have implemented some forms of code of practice
